openings.decision: DISPUTE (optional flag: A and B optional, C scored). Decided OPTIONAL from the drawing. The door stands in the master bathroom's glass screen, not in a wall: 10 mm glass on layer 0 (lines x 9.5116 / 9.5216) between two 0.10 m layer-0 kerb lines (4EE8 x 9.4666, 4EE5 x 9.5666) that run on unbroken past the door; the glass stops at y 5.3507 and restarts at y 6.0507 (the 0.70 m leaf). It is drawn exactly like the two shower doors on the same screen line (SR-20, SR-21): 10 mm glass leaf open 30 deg (A-DOOR 5A8D / 5A8F), dashed 30 deg swing on A-DOOR-HDLN (5A91), handle outline on A-GENM-HDLN, no A-DOOR-FRAM frame (every hinged and pocket door in a wall has 4 to 18 frame lines within 0.12 m; only the bi-fold and the four glass-screen doors have none), and it is one of the four exploded copies of the same unused shower-door family (IN_SHOWER DOOR1 - Shower door_700X2160MM). The compartment behind it (x 9.57-11.49, y 5.25-6.94) holds only the WC: an enclosure inside the master bathroom. The earlier keys list a shower screen as a glass wall with its door part of the enclosure (Sukhumvit, shared definition of 26 Oct) and toilet cubicle doors as optional (tower), and the three lists agree that the other three doors of these screens are optional; so this one is optional too (not scored either way). Ends as all three lists (the gap in the glass, 0.70 m). If the 3D team wants doors in glass screens scored, set optional false here (and on SR-20 to SR-22); the ends need no change.

Glass screen across the room east of the BOH (glass y 4.770-4.780 between 0.10 m lines y 4.724 / 4.824): fixed 0.10 + door SR-22 + 1.095.

West bay of the master bedroom: three curtain-wall facets (SR-25..SR-27), between the west wall pieces A-WALL 541E/541D (ends y 2.86-2.93) and 541C/541F (y 8.79-8.86). a/b here only mark the bay's extent.

Five north bays (SR-28..SR-42), each three curtain-wall facets (0.707 / 1.417 / 0.707 m panes at 75 / 30 / 165 deg) from the end of a 0.10 m straight facade wall to the top of a 1.7-1.8 m solid angled facade wall; a/b here only mark the extent of the row.

uncertain.what: SR-19, the glass door of the WC compartment, is optional (dispute decided: a door of the bathroom glass screen, drawn as the shower doors). If the 3D team wants doors in glass screens scored regardless of the room, set optional false on SR-19 to SR-22 (ends 0.70 m by the leaf need no change); then the key has 20 scored openings.

Doors outside the suite: the four corridor doors SR-13 to SR-16 (two riser doors, two doors of neighbouring units) are scored, as all three lists did (like the tower key's shaft doors); SR-17 / SR-18 are optional because the view crop cuts them. If the key is meant to cover the suite only, SR-13 to SR-16 become optional (12 scored openings).

SR-17 / SR-18: the two D22 service double doors at the east edge are cut by the crop at x 25.079; only 1.092 m of each 1.80 m opening is drawn. The key keeps the nominal 1.80 m (centre at the block insert point); a detector can only see x 23.987-25.079. Optional either way.

SR-03, the bi-fold door of the walk-in wardrobe (2.225 m, the full wall gap; the dashed track spans the same), is scored as a room door by all three lists. If walk-in wardrobes are read as casework it would be optional.

Curtain-wall bays: listed per straight facet as 18 optional windows (all three lists), ends at the wall material that bounds each facet (straight facade wall ends, Walls 13 corner wedges, angled solid walls). Other readings: one window per bay (e.g. north bay 1 chord (3.8475, 11.4961)-(6.1244, 12.8110), west bay x 2.797 from y 2.894 to 8.824) or glass wall only (the tower key). None is scored either way.

Width convention: every door is measured between the faces of the wall ends with the 50 mm A-DOOR-FRAM frames inside the opening (1.10 for the pocket doors, 0.80 / 0.75 / 1.00 for the hinged ones). The clear width between the frames is 0.10 m less (0.05 m less for SR-06), which for the 0.80 m and 1.00 m doors (SR-05, SR-09, SR-10, SR-12, SR-15, SR-16) is exactly the scorer's width limit (max(0.10 m, 10 %)): a detection measured between the frames passes or fails there on rounding.

The corridor-alcove mouths (C-40, C-43) are rejected. A passage detected at a mouth is an extra; if the unit door behind it (SR-15 / SR-16) is not detected, the scorer pairs the door with such a passage (centres exactly 0.30 m apart, its centre limit) and fails it on width (1.175 vs 1.00).

SR-23 and SR-24 (open sides of the dressing area and of the lobby of bedroom 2) are optional passage mouths: a wall end facing a cross wall that holds a pocket door at that point. They could also be read as no opening at all.
SR-06 (small room south of the foyer): 0.75 m between the wall fills, but the frame on its east side stands 0.05 m inside the wall stub; leaf 0.70. Lists agree on 0.75.

Floor tag: the key's floor is 'suite_revit' (drawing.json floor_tag; tools/prims.py tags every item of this one-plan drawing with the cache name). The detector writes each opening's floor as the name the mapping's "floors" entry gives the area 'suite_revit' (openings.py run()). The mapping lies in the blind-run folder, which this step does not read; if it names the floor differently, rename the key's floor (or the output's) before scoring, since score.py pairs per floor string.
